headline: 7 New Claude Features for Dev Workflows
summary: Anthropic shipped seven new Claude capabilities designed to embed AI deeper into daily engineering routines. The update targets context handling, tool integration, and team collaboration — moving beyond chat into true IDE-native assistance.

slides.title: Why Does AI Still Feel Disconnected From Your Editor?
slides.subtitle: Seven new Claude features close the gap between chat and code.
slides.body: You switch tabs, copy context, paste errors, and hope the model understands your codebase. Anthropic's latest drop targets that exact friction — seven features built to live inside your workflow, not beside it.
slides.deep_dive: Most AI coding assistants operate as external chat windows. They lack persistent awareness of your project structure, build state, or runtime behavior. This forces developers into a context-shuttling loop: extract snippets, explain intent, validate suggestions, re-apply. Anthropic's update rethinks this by embedding reasoning, tooling, and memory directly into the developer loop — treating the IDE as a first-class runtime, not a text source.
slides.key_fact: Seven new features announced; all aim to reduce context-switching between IDE and AI.
slides.why_it_matters: Eliminates the copy-paste tax that makes AI feel like a separate tool instead of a teammate.

slides.title: From Chat Companion to Workflow Native
slides.subtitle: Features span context, tools, memory, and team sharing.
slides.body: The release covers persistent project memory, native tool execution, cross-file reasoning, shared team contexts, cost-aware routing, offline-capable caching, and IDE-level diff previews. Each targets a specific workflow break point.
slides.deep_dive: Previous Claude interactions were stateless — each conversation started fresh. The new features introduce a layered architecture: a project index that builds semantic understanding of your codebase, a tool runtime that executes commands and reads outputs, a memory layer that persists decisions across sessions, and a team namespace for shared context. Pricing tiers gate some capabilities: Free gets basic memory and caching; Pro adds tool execution and diff previews; Team unlocks shared contexts and admin controls.
slides.key_fact: Features distributed across Free, Pro, and Team tiers — not all available on every plan.
slides.why_it_matters: You can now match Claude's capability tier to your team's workflow maturity and budget.

slides.title: How Claude Now Processes Your Codebase
slides.subtitle: Index → Reason → Act → Remember → Share
slides.body: A background indexer builds a semantic map. Queries trigger targeted retrieval. Tools execute in a sandbox. Results update the memory layer. Team members inherit context automatically.
slides.deep_dive: The indexer doesn't just embed files — it parses ASTs, resolves imports, tracks symbol references, and builds a call graph. When you ask a question, the retriever walks this graph to pull only relevant context, not entire files. The tool runtime spins up ephemeral containers with your project's dependencies pre-installed, runs commands, captures stdout/stderr, and feeds results back into the reasoning loop. The memory layer stores decisions ("use library X for auth") as structured facts, not chat history. Team sync merges these facts across members with conflict resolution.
slides.key_fact: Semantic code graph enables surgical context retrieval instead of brute-force file dumps.
slides.why_it_matters: Token efficiency and relevance improve dramatically — the model sees what matters, not everything.

slides.title: Editor → Local Agent → Code Index → Compiler/LLM
slides.subtitle: Four-layer stack keeps latency low and context fresh.
slides.body: A lightweight IDE extension talks to a local agent. The agent maintains the semantic index. The compiler/LLM layer executes tools and reasons. All state syncs to cloud for team sharing.
slides.deep_dive: The local agent is the keystone — it runs in-process with your editor, giving it instant access to unsaved buffers, cursor position, and git status. It incrementally updates the semantic index on every keystroke using a differential AST parser. The compiler/LLM layer is decoupled: it can run locally (for privacy/offline) or route to cloud (for heavier reasoning). Tool execution happens in project-matched containers spun up by the agent. Team sync uses CRDTs on the fact layer — no central server bottleneck for reads.
slides.key_fact: Local agent enables zero-latency context; cloud layer handles heavy reasoning and team sync.
slides.why_it_matters: Architecture separates hot-path context (local) from compute-intensive reasoning (flexible).

slides.title: Developer Intent → Structured Artifact
slides.subtitle: Natural language becomes verified diff, not suggestion.
slides.body: You describe a change. The system retrieves context, plans edits, runs tools to validate, and presents a reviewable diff. Acceptance commits to memory and index.
slides.deep_dive: The input isn't just text — it's intent enriched with implicit context: current file, test failures, recent commits, team conventions. The planner decomposes intent into atomic edits mapped to the semantic graph. Each edit runs through the tool sandbox: type-check, lint, test. Failures feed back into the planner for revision. The output is a structured diff with metadata: affected symbols, test coverage delta, migration notes. One-click apply stages changes in git. The fact layer records "refactored auth to use library X" — future queries inherit this knowledge.
slides.key_fact: Output is a verified, reviewable diff with test evidence — not a raw code block to vet manually.
slides.why_it_matters: Closes the verify-then-apply loop that consumes 60% of AI-assisted coding time.

slides.processing: Semantic retrieval → edit planning → tool validation (type/lint/test) → revision loop

slides.title: Antipatterns That Waste the New Capabilities
slides.subtitle: Treat it like chat and you'll miss 80% of the value.
slides.body: Don't paste code snippets — the index already knows. Don't ask for whole files — request surgical edits. Don't ignore team facts — they encode tribal knowledge. Don't skip diff review — validation is the feature.
slides.deep_dive: The biggest mistake is treating the new Claude like the old chat model. Pasted context pollutes the semantic graph with stale snapshots. Requesting full-file rewrites bypasses the surgical edit planner and triggers unnecessary token spend. Ignoring team facts means relearning decisions your colleagues already encoded. Skipping diff review defeats the validated-artifact guarantee — the tool sandbox catches errors, but human intent verification remains essential. Pro tip: use "explain this decision" queries to surface team facts before coding. Pro tip: bind "accept diff" to a keyboard shortcut — the workflow is designed for speed.
slides.key_fact: Pasting context, requesting full rewrites, and skipping diff review are the top three value-destroying habits.
slides.why_it_matters: The architecture rewards surgical, validated, team-aware interactions — not chat-style prompting.

slides.title: From Zero to Power User in Three Steps
slides.subtitle: Install, index, iterate — team onboarding is automatic.
slides.body: Install the IDE extension. Open a project — indexing starts automatically. Ask a real task. Share the workspace with your team. Follow @vijayakumarj_ai for daily AI engineering updates.
slides.deep_dive: The extension installs in under a minute (VS Code, JetBrains, Neovim supported). First index takes seconds for small projects, minutes for monorepos — runs in background, no blocking. Your first query should be a real task: "add error handling to the payment flow" or "migrate this component to the new design system." Watch the diff, review test results, accept. Invite teammates via the Team panel — they inherit the index and facts instantly. Tier upgrade is in-app: Free → Pro → Team unlocks progressively. Documentation lives in the extension's help menu with interactive tutorials.
slides.key_fact: Zero-config start; team onboarding is one click; tier upgrades are in-app.
slides.why_it_matters: No infrastructure setup, no context engineering — the tool adapts to your existing project.
